note: Reply drafts for measuring the guardrail (python -m evals.guardrail_eval). Each case gives a real ticket, the clause ids treated as retrieved in that run, whether the customer's account record was looked up, and any refund amounts proposed; then a drafted reply and its label: the hallucinated-policy errors it truly contains. Labels say what is TRUE, not what the checker will find. Kinds: unsupported_fact (a figure grounded nowhere), miscited_fact (a real figure attributed to a cited clause that does not contain it), citation_not_retrieved (cites a clause not retrieved), blind_spot (a real error with no checkable figure in it - the deterministic guardrail cannot see these by design, and they are here to measure that). Two clean cases state true figures the checker cannot ground (a computed per-seat price, a paraphrased threshold); they are labelled clean so their false positives count. Drafted by the assistant AFTER the checker was written, so the checkable cases are an upper-bound sanity check, not an independent measurement - see ADR 0007. Set reviewed to true only after the label owner has checked every case against the corpus.
